turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have a yield strength CLOSEST to 1051 MPa — not the highest, the closest to that value — then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning

**Step 1 — Key observation about the target.** The training set's yield strengths range from ~140 MPa up to a maximum of ~908 MPa (908.5, 899.2, 863.9 are the top three). Since **no training recipe reaches 1051 MPa**, and the pool candidates are drawn from the same recipe space, "closest to 1051 MPa" effectively means **selecting the candidates with the highest predicted strength**.

**Step 2 — What drives high strength in the training data.**
- **Heat treatment:** `quench_temper` dominates the high end (most targets >650 MPa are quench_temper); `annealed` is consistently weak; `quenched` is mid-low.
- **Route:** wrought is most often on top; cast/AM can also score high with the right recipe.
- **Processing:** long aging time (>30 h) and moderate aging temp (~480–650 °C) correlate with high strength; very short aging (<5 h) is penalized.
- **Composition:** extreme alloying is penalized — C ≈ 1.2, Al ≈ 2.0, Ti ≈ 1.5, Nb ≈ 1.0, Mo = 6 all appear repeatedly in the lowest-strength rows. Moderate Cr/Ni with some Co and V is fine or beneficial.

**Step 3 — Nearest-neighbor matching to the strongest training rows.**
- **c079** is nearly a duplicate of the **strongest training sample (908.5 MPa)**: quench_temper/AM, C≈0.4, Cr≈5, Mo≈1.3, V≈1.5, Co≈10.9, Cu≈2.4, aging ≈600 °C, time ≈45 h, cooling ≈37 — almost every field matches. Predicted ≈ 900 MPa → closest possible to 1051.
- **c017** is nearly a duplicate of the **863.9 MPa row**: quench_temper/wrought, Cr≈7.7, Ni≈10.1, low Al/Ti, aging ≈529 °C, time ≈49 h. Predicted ≈ 850–870 MPa.
- **c009** closely resembles the 908.5 MPa sample too (Co≈10.6, V≈1.24, Cu≈2.3, quench_temper, aging 559 °C, 41 h), differing mainly in lower Cr/Ni; supported by similar Co-rich quench_temper rows at 617–625 MPa even with poor aging times. Predicted ≈ 750–850 MPa.
- **c008** is nearly identical to the **737.7 MPa row** (quench_temper/cast, Cr≈16, C≈0.35, Al≈1.3, aging ≈550 °C, ~19 h). Predicted ≈ 730–740 MPa. (c033 is a near-equal twin of the same row.)
- **c094** closely matches the **734.1 MPa row** (quench_temper/wrought, C≈0.24, Cr≈6, Ni≈8, aging ≈513 °C) but with an even longer aging time (50 h). Predicted ≈ 730–750 MPa.

Other candidates (c039 ≈ 721.6-MPa twin, c033, c097, c088) are strong but land slightly below these five; most remaining pool entries either use annealed/quenched treatments, extreme solute levels, or very short aging, all of which map to <650 MPa in training.

**Final: c079, c017, c009, c008, c094**
